plain_english_policy: This bill (HB381, 2012) modifies Alabama’s state employee retirement and health insurance benefits to **specifically recognize hazardous duty time for correctional officers** as creditable service under the Employees’ Retirement System (ERS) and Teachers’ Retirement System (TRS). It does not alter general pension formulas but adds a targeted adjustment for correctional officers retiring after December 31, 2012. The policy direction is to **increase retirement benefits for correctional officers** by counting hazardous duty time toward years of service for health insurance premium subsidies—effectively reducing retiree out-of-pocket costs.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The bill would create a **progressive benefit enhancement** for correctional officers by treating their hazardous duty time as equivalent to one year of service per five years served in corrections. This would likely result in higher employer-subsidized health insurance contributions for these retirees, reducing their premium burden. The policy prioritizes **public safety personnel recognition** and aligns with broader trends of compensating high-risk occupations for service under retirement systems.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill’s text explicitly targets correctional officers, implying a legislative intent to **acknowledge their hazardous work conditions** and incentivize retention through improved retirement benefits. No broader ideological stance is inferred beyond this targeted adjustment.
evidence_quotes: For an employee who has elected to participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Plan (DROP) as defined under Sections 16-25-150 and 36-27-170, ...

(g) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (a), **the calculation of the employer contribution for correction officers, retiring after December 31, 2012, shall include credit for any hazardous duty time awarded under the Employees’ Retirement System or the Teachers’ Retirement System**...
provided that the agency from which a correctional officer retires shall reimburse the board for the cost of any credited hazardous duty time
review_reason: The bill’s intent is clear and unambiguous: it modifies health insurance premium subsidies to include hazardous duty time for correctional officers. No further context or interpretation is required.
